Hello everyone, I am Yu Bingqi, a Ph.D. in mathematics from Jilin University. My main research direction is Hamiltonian systems. Here I sincerely submit to the lean community the result of my recent first attempt at lean formalization-the formalization of the KAM theorem. We mainly refer to Arnold's original paper in 1963 and did a formal project of the KAM theorem for finite-dimensional non-degenerate analysis.The tools used include Lean4.33.1, mathlib v4.33.1, which includes its own independent formalization of multivariate complex analysis, KAM iteration, analytical invariant torus, resonance measurement estimation, and less content in the mathlib library. The author's semantic self-examination and audit examples have been completed, but they have not undergone independent peer review.I used AI assistance when writing Lean files, and it has been publicly explained in the warehouse.:
GitHub：https://github.com/ybq1415926-droid/arnold1963-kam
Zenodo v1.0.0：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23232025
The exact theorem description can be found in the warehouse docs/Arnold1963_Main_Theorem_Code_Aligned_EN.pdf found
This topic was moved here from #Project announcements > KAM in Lean 4 by Michael Rothgang.
